summary: Patch tries to make backward rename restore the old auto-generated name, but for an unnamed (old_fields) index self.old_name is None and the auto-generated name is never stored in state, so `get_index_by_name(self.old_name)` cannot recover it. Django's actual fix kept backward as a no-op for old_fields and instead made forward re-detect the current index by column via `_constraint_names`, making re-apply idempotent-safe; this approach is the wrong abstraction.

issues.description: For the unnamed/unique_together case (old_fields set), self.old_name is None, so `new_index = from_model_state.get_index_by_name(self.old_name)` calls get_index_by_name(None), which raises 'No index named None'. The auto-generated old index name is not stored in ModelState.options['indexes'] (only the forward-added Index named self.new_name is), so the target name simply cannot be reconstructed from state this way. Correct approach detects the DB index by columns via schema_editor._constraint_names, as done in the forward path.

Because the target (old auto-generated) name is unrecoverable from state, the backward operation cannot actually rename the index back for the exact reported scenario (unnamed index for unique_together), so the crash-on-re-apply bug is not correctly resolved. The forward path is left untouched, so idempotency of re-apply is not addressed at its real source.

Renaming inside database_backwards for old_fields diverges from Django's chosen design (backward = no-op, forward re-detects by column). Even if it happened to satisfy a narrow test, it is special-cased rather than a general, column-based fix.
